---
title: "Draft: import metabolomics QC/blank/standard files into GLAMR"
---

**This is a draft, not a live import chunk.** It is not run against the real
GLAMR repository from this dev sandbox (per instruction, nothing in
~/GLAMR/`/nfs/turbo/lsa-kiledal/GLAMR` was touched this session). Copy the
chunk below into GLAMR's real `code/import.Rmd`, immediately after the
existing "Metabolomics data for USGS / GLERL (set_41)" chunk
(`code/import.Rmd:1671-1745` as of this writing), then run it there.

## What this imports

`import/staging/202407_metabolomics_from_usgs/newdata11212024/{2016..2020}/`
holds 272 files that exist on disk but were never assigned sample IDs or
imported: `blank1`-`blank28`, `QC_A_*` (pooled QC), `QC_SA_*` (spiked pool),
and `LCTXM0_01`-`LCTXM5_0` (an 11-point microcystin calibration curve), per
batch year. These are exactly the QC infrastructure the metabolomics
pipeline's blank filtering, drift correction, and (phase 2) targeted
quantification need - without them the pipeline can run but everything QC-
related in `pipelines/metabolomics.smk`'s `metab_feature_qc` rule degrades to
"skipped, no blanks/QC pools in manifest" (which it will already do
gracefully if you don't import these, but you'd lose real functionality
for no reason).

## Generalized import convention

The existing metabolomics import chunk symlinks a single fixed name,
`data/omics/metabolomes/{SampleID}/spectra/raw_spectra.raw`. This assumes
every file is Thermo `.raw`, which is true for set_41 but won't generalize
to a future Agilent/Bruker/Sciex/Waters project (Waters `.raw` is even a
*directory*, not a file, so a bare extension can't tell the vendor apart
from Thermo's file-based `.raw`). The pipeline's Snakemake rules
(`pipelines/metabolomics.smk`, rules `metab_convert_thermo` /
`metab_convert_vendor` / `metab_mzml_passthrough`) route conversion by
looking for `raw_spectra.{vendor}.{ext}`, where `{vendor}` comes from
`pypelib.metabolomics.detect_format.detect()` - the same format-detection
logic this dev sandbox validated against 9 real/synthetic vendor cases
(Thermo, Bruker, Agilent, Waters, Sciex, Shimadzu, mzML, and two ambiguous/
unsupported cases that correctly raise a clear error). **Any future import
chunk, including this one, should call the same detector rather than
re-deriving vendor tags by hand**, so format routing has one source of
truth. This chunk shells out to the installed `metab-detect-format` CLI
(`pyproject.toml`'s `[project.scripts]` entry, added alongside this
pipeline) for that reason.

```{r}
library(unglue)

# Newly-imported samples continue the real samp_ sequence. As of this
# writing the highest assigned metabolome sample is samp_11655 (the 352
# already-imported set_41 files, samp_11304-11655) - confirm before running:
#   tail -n +2 import/staging/202407_metabolomics_from_usgs/glamr_import_table.tsv |
#     cut -f8 | sed 's/samp_//' | sort -n | tail -1
next_start_id <- 11656

file_info <- Sys.glob("import/staging/202407_metabolomics_from_usgs/newdata11212024/*/*.raw") %>%
  data.frame(path = .) %>%
  unglue_unnest(
    path,
    "import/staging/202407_metabolomics_from_usgs/newdata11212024/{year}/{SampleName}.raw",
    remove = FALSE
  ) %>%
  type_convert() %>%
  mutate(filename = basename(path),
         sample_type = "metabolome",
         StudyID = "set_41",
         file_size = fs::file_size(path)) %>%
  arrange(year, SampleName) %>%
  mutate(SampleID = paste0("samp_", next_start_id + row_number() - 1)) %>%
  write_tsv("import/staging/202407_metabolomics_from_usgs/glamr_import_table_qc.tsv")

# Detect vendor format per file (all Thermo .raw for this batch, but this
# generalizes automatically - see note above)
file_info <- file_info %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  mutate(vendor = system2("metab-detect-format", shQuote(path), stdout = TRUE) %>%
           str_extract("(?<=vendor: ).*")) %>%
  ungroup()

import_files <- file_info %>%
  mutate(import_file_path = str_glue("import/{sample_type}s/{SampleID}.raw"),
         link_path = str_glue("../../{path}"),
         raw_files = str_glue("{SampleID}.raw"))

fs::link_create(import_files$link_path, import_files$import_file_path)

## Actually import data

import_table <- import_files %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  mutate(staged_read_fp = glue("import/{sample_type}s/{raw_files}"),
         staged_reads_present = fs::file_exists(staged_read_fp),
         sample_dir = glue("data/omics/{sample_type}s/{SampleID}"),
         raw_reads_dir = glue("{sample_dir}/spectra"),
         # vendor-tagged filename, not the fixed "raw_spectra.raw" the
         # existing set_41 chunk uses - see note above
         imported_read_fp = str_glue("{sample_dir}/spectra/raw_spectra.{vendor}.raw"),
         previously_imported = file.exists(imported_read_fp))

new_imports <- import_table %>%
  filter(previously_imported == FALSE,
         staged_reads_present == TRUE)

mapply(dir.create, base::unique(new_imports$raw_reads_dir),
       MoreArgs = list(recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE))

fs::link_create(paste0("../../../../../", new_imports$staged_read_fp),
                 new_imports$imported_read_fp)

## Link into project folders (already exists: data/projects/set_41/metabolomes/)

project_dirs <- new_imports %>%
  mutate(proj_and_type_dir = glue("data/projects/{StudyID}/{sample_type}s/"),
         project_sample_data_dir = glue("data/projects/{StudyID}/{sample_type}s/{SampleID}"),
         link_path = glue("../../../../{sample_dir}"))

simple_dirs <- project_dirs %>%
  select(sample_dir, proj_and_type_dir, project_sample_data_dir, link_path) %>%
  distinct()

file.symlink(simple_dirs$link_path, simple_dirs$project_sample_data_dir)

## Write to import log

old_imports <- read_tsv("data/import_log.tsv") %>%
  mutate(F_primer = as.character(F_primer))

import_check <- new_imports %>%
  mutate(import_sucess = file.exists(imported_read_fp),
         import_time = date())

all_imports <- bind_rows(old_imports, import_check)
write_tsv(all_imports, "data/import_log.tsv", col_names = TRUE)
```

## After running: populate `ms_role` in the pipeline manifest

The metabolomics pipeline's `checkpoint metab_run_manifest` auto-guesses
`ms_role` from the filename (`blank*` -> blank, `QC_A_*` -> qc_pool,
`QC_SA_*` -> qc_spike, `LCTXM*` -> cal_standard) and writes
`data/projects/{dataset}/metabolomics/run_manifest.tsv`. Verified against
real data in this dev sandbox: for the 2016 batch (54 samples + 40 QC
files) the guesses came out exactly right (54 sample / 15 blank / 11
cal_standard / 9 qc_pool / 5 qc_spike) with no manual correction needed.
Spot-check `run_manifest.tsv` after the pipeline's first run per dataset
regardless - a filename convention this clean is set_41-specific, not
guaranteed for future projects.

## Note: `GLR_ID-*` <-> `bios_*`/metagenome linking is still unsolved

None of this addresses the fact that all 624 metabolome samples (352 + 272
from this chunk) have `BioSampleID = NULL` and that `GLR_ID-*` USGS sample
names appear nowhere in the `Great_Lakes_Omics_Datasets.xlsx` metadata
workbook. That's a metadata problem (need a USGS/GLERL crosswalk), not a
code problem, and is out of scope for both this import chunk and the
pipeline itself - see the plan's "Cross-omics linking (deferred)" section.
